title: Red blocks, yellow letters and a toy soldier
label: Brand gallery
lede: The Kay-Bee of the 1980s had a toy soldier for a mascot. The KB of the 1990s and 2000s had red block capitals and a yellow “toys” with a spiral in the o. Here are the marks as they survive, a store as it stands now, and our drawings in the same spirit.

archive.caption: The last K·B Toys logo, as shown on the website while the brand was for sale.
archive.credit: Cropped from an Internet Archive capture of kbtoys.com dated Aug 1, 2009. Shown for commentary; trademarks belong to their owners.

archive.caption: A doll of the Kay-Bee toy soldier mascot. The photograph is undated.
A former KB Toys storefront at Rivergate Mall, Goodlettsville, Tennessee, gate down and sign removed, as described by the photographer.
archive.credit: Photo: Larry Hachucka, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:VINTAGE_Former_KB_Toys;_Rivergate_Mall;_Goodletsville_TN.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.
